interface.title: msannot — Annotation de petites molécules par spectres MS/MS (Streamlit dashboard, v0.1.1)
interface.field: Metabolomics / analytical chemistry (tandem mass spectrometry, small-molecule annotation)
interface.stage_of_work: Data analysis: annotating measured MS/MS spectra against a reference library, and judging how reliable the annotation is
interface.what_it_is_for: Search a query MS/MS spectrum against a curated MassBank library by identity or analogue search with cosine, modified cosine or spectral entropy, then review ranked hits, a mirror plot, the proposed structure and benchmark statistics on how reliable such matches are.

data.note: The bundled MassBank demo library loaded by default: 23,491 spectra, 3,958 compounds, 24 labs. I used the 3 built-in example queries (caffeine, carbamazepine, venlafaxine). I also uploaded the test file example_queries.mgf (2 spectra: caffeine and carbamazepine) through 'Fichier MGF/MSP', and typed a hand-made carbamazepine peak list into 'Pics collés'. The Benchmark tab was already filled from an 'msannot demo' run dated 2026-10-31 06:42 UTC. The UI is in French.

features.name: Three-way query input (example / file / pasted peak list)
features.general: Let the user provide the item to analyse by picking a bundled example, uploading a file of several items and choosing one, or typing values by hand, with a minimum-content check before analysis runs
features.specific: The Source radio switches between Exemples (dropdown of 3 MassBank queries), Fichier MGF/MSP (upload, then a Spectre dropdown listing the file's spectra) and Pics collés (precursor m/z and a 'm/z intensité' text area). Fewer than 5 peaks after cleaning blocks the search with a warning.
steps: Choose a source with the Source radio
Pick an example, or upload an MGF/MSP file, or type a precursor m/z and a peak list
Choose the spectrum to search in the Spectre dropdown
Fix the input if it is too sparse (fewer than 5 peaks gives a warning)
serves_tasks: Type in a measurement by hand

features.name: Library search with selectable mode, metric and tolerances
features.general: Run a similarity search of one item against a reference collection, choosing same-mass or related-item mode, the similarity measure, how many results to return and how strict the pre-filters are, and get a ranked, exportable table
features.specific: Sidebar Paramètres: Mode Identification/Analogues, Mesure (Cosine, Modified cosine, Entropie spectrale), Résultats slider 1–25, Fenêtre de précurseur (ppm), Écart de masse maximal (Da). Any change reruns the search, and the hit table (rank, identifier, name, inchikey14, smiles, contributor, precursor_mz, delta_mz, score, n_matches, tanimoto) can be downloaded as hits.tsv.
steps: Choose Identification or Analogues
Choose the similarity measure
Set the number of results and the ppm / Da windows
Read the ranked hit table (scroll right for n_matches and tanimoto if the window is narrow)
Download the hits as TSV
serves_tasks: Find same-mass candidates and rank them by spectral similarity
Compare scoring methods on the same unknown
Adjust how many candidates are returned and how strictly mass must match

features.name: Mirror plot with hit picker and paired structures
features.general: Pick one candidate from a ranked list and see it drawn against the query, top versus bottom, with matching features highlighted and a summary of agreement, next to both chemical structures
features.specific: 'Spectre miroir du résultat n°' dropdown → static matplotlib mirror plot (query above, library hit below; blue = matched peak, orange = 'Apparié par décalage' for modified cosine, grey = unmatched), title showing metric score · matched peaks · Tanimoto · Δ précurseur, RDKit drawings of the query and hit structures, and the 'Structure proposée' panel that follows the selected hit
steps: Run a search to fill the hit list
Choose a rank in 'Spectre miroir du résultat n°'
Read the mirror plot and its score, peak-count, Tanimoto and Δ mass line
Compare the query and result structures and read the proposed structure
serves_tasks: Compare the unknown with one candidate peak by peak
See the structure the candidate implies

features.name: Leave-one-out analogue search (simulate an unknown)
features.general: Hide the known answer from the reference collection to test what the method proposes when the true item is absent, and score how structurally close the proposal is
features.specific: Mode 'Analogues' plus the 'Exclure le composé de la requête (simule une inconnue)' checkbox removes the query compound's InChIKey from the library. Candidates within ±'Écart de masse maximal' Da are ranked, and each gets a Tanimoto (Morgan) similarity to the true structure. Venlafaxine gives O-desmethylvenlafaxine (Tanimoto 0.72) with modified cosine but MEX (0.13) with entropy (replayed at the 200 Da default); uploaded caffeine gives theobromine.
steps: Switch Mode to Analogues
Tick 'Exclure le composé de la requête'
Optionally narrow 'Écart de masse maximal (Da)'
Compare metrics and read the tanimoto column and mirror plot (shift-matched peaks in orange)
serves_tasks: Find structurally related candidates when the true compound is missing
Check whether another scoring method proposes a better or worse relative

features.name: Reference-collection overview with name filter
features.general: Summarise a reference collection with headline count and distribution plots, then filter its record table by name and choose which columns to show
features.specific: Bibliothèque tab: spectrum count metric, figure with precursor m/z histogram, peaks-per-spectrum histogram and top-10 labs, 'Filtrer par nom de composé' substring filter with a match count (first 500 shown), and dataframe toolbar (show/hide columns, CSV download, search, fullscreen)
steps: Open the Bibliothèque tab and read the count and composition plots
Type a compound name in the filter
Read the match count and filtered table
Show or hide columns (e.g. hide smiles to bring instrument_type, collision_energy, license into view)
serves_tasks: See the size and makeup of the reference collection
Check whether a given compound and its relatives are covered

features.name: Benchmark report with confidence intervals and baselines
features.general: Present precomputed method-evaluation results as sortable tables with confidence intervals and random/oracle baselines, plus charts for accuracy by scenario, score calibration and structural agreement
features.specific: Benchmark tab: Identification (top-1) table by setting × subset × metric with top1_ci_low/high and random_top1. Analogues table with median Tanimoto and close-analogue fraction and their CIs for cosine/modified cosine/entropy/random/oracle. Bar chart with error bars, calibration curves (precision and coverage against a score threshold), Tanimoto cumulative curves, Tanimoto-vs-score curve, and a GNPS-style molecular network with an edge-Tanimoto histogram.
steps: Open the Benchmark tab
Read and sort the identification table (e.g. by top1)
Compare all labs vs other labs, and all queries vs queries with same-mass competitors, against the random baseline
Read the analogue table and curves
Open a figure fullscreen
serves_tasks: Read accuracy with uncertainty, overall and in harder conditions
Read how good relative-finding is and how score relates to trustworthiness
